title: John Stones exit from Manchester City set to be announced next week
content:
John Stones will leave Manchester City upon the expiration of his contract this summer, with an announcement expected to be communicated next week.

The mutual decision will bring an end to the 31-year-old’s close to a decade-long stay at the club, where he has won 16 trophies including six league titles and the 2023 Champions League.

The centre-back has, however, been hampered by injury issues across the past several seasons and has made more than 30 appearances in just one of the past five seasons.

In 2025-26, the former Everton defender has started in just four Premier League matches for Pep Guardiola’s side.

It is anticipated that a number of top clubs across Europe will be interested in a summer move for the central defender.

Stones, who was called-up to Thomas Tuchel’s England squad in the March international break and has won 87 caps, will hope to feature at this summer’s World Cup.

City have strengthened in central defence in recent transfer windows, signing Marc Guehi in January having 12 months earlier added Abdukodir Khusanov and Vitor Reis, who has subsequently been on loan at City Football Group sister club Girona in La Liga.

Prior to joining Manchester City, Stones spent three-and-a-half years at Everton, whom he joined from Barnsley in January 2013. He played 95 times for the Merseyside club.

Stones is the second player who will be leaving City as a free agent this summer, with Bernardo Silva — who joined from Monaco in 2017 — also bringing an end to his stay in Manchester.

This should be taken as a measure of how good Stones is rather than disparaging of what he has achieved at City, but there is a sense of sadness that accompanies Stones’ departure because it feels like he was always capable of so much more.

That is, of course, due to injury. Stones’ class and importance to City was writ large during the 2022-23 season, where he was absolutely integral as Guardiola’s team won the treble. His dual role, starting at centre-back and moving right the way through midfield up to the edge of the opposition box, was essentially the key that unlocked City that season, helping them accommodate Erling Haaland while ensuring they retained the control of matches that was always so important.

Stones was magnificent in that role, one that he looked born to do. His natural grace and confidence in possession always marked him out as a rare centre-back, and those traits were given a proper platform higher up on the pitch.

The sadness is that he has only sporadically been seen since then, with injuries keeping him out of the majority of the past two seasons in particular. Remarkably, that 22-23 campaign was essentially the only one of his 10 at City, to date, where he has featured regularly in the run-in. In 2020-21 he was ever present in the team that got to the Champions League final, but missed league three games in May. But that season, like the vast majority of his City career, has been blighted by injuries.

Stones has of course shown everybody how good he is over the course of his 292 appearance for City, and he leaves the Etihad having contributed to 16 trophies, but that ability could have been put to even greater use had he not regularly struggled with injuries. He has done enough to be regarded as one of the best centre-backs of the Premier League era, but he really could have been the greatest.
